tasks.short: Match supplier invoices to purchase orders and goods receipts in AFAS, chase the ones that don't match.

today.trigger: A supplier invoice arrives by mail, as a PDF or UBL file, in the AP inbox.
steps: Open the invoice and look up the purchase order and goods receipt in AFAS Profit
Compare quantities, prices and totals line by line
Email the site or buyer in Outlook when a receipt is missing or the price differs
Record the match and send the invoice for approval
drudgery: Chasing site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo for missing goods receipts
today.time_sinks: Most time goes into the minority of invoices that don't match and the email back-and-forth to find out why.

lenses.faster: AFAS matches UBL and one-to-one PDF invoices against order and receipt and posts them itself; the bookkeeper only handles the exception list, which a short model-written reason per mismatch makes quicker to work through.
lenses.autonomous: An incoming invoice triggers capture, matching against the order within the set tolerance, and posting with approval for payment; mismatches outside tolerance go to the bookkeeper's queue.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: price and quantity differences per supplier are checked against contract prices on every invoice, not just when someone notices, and reported to purchasing monthly; demand would grow because purchasing wants this data.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses ticking off line totals; bookkeepers want more time to fix supplier master data and sort out problem suppliers.
lenses.options: Little room for scenarios; the one real choice is the tolerance level per supplier group, where two or three settings can be tested against last quarter's invoices.
lenses.altitude: The week moves from matching to setting tolerances and match rules with the controller and keeping supplier data clean; the job gets more expert in procurement controls.
reach: Take over contract price checks from purchasing, learning to read supply contracts
Supplier master data upkeep normally done ad hoc by the Controller

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which site manager to call, judging whether a price difference is a real error or an agreed change, and deciding when to pay part of an invoice.
tasks.pattern_why: Three-way match on order, receipt and invoice is a set of rules AFAS already runs; only PDF capture needs a model, which AFAS Scan & herken covers.

in_practice.trigger: Invoice received in AFAS (UBL via Peppol or PDF in the scan inbox).
steps: AFAS reads the invoice to line level and finds the supplier by KvK, VAT number and IBAN
Rules match against order and goods receipt within tolerance
Matched invoices are posted and approved for payment
Mismatches land in the exception queue with the difference shown
Bookkeeper resolves, adjusts or rejects
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper decides on every invoice outside tolerance; the Controller signs off tolerance changes.
data_needed: Supplier master data with IBAN and KvK
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS invoice workflow history, with match result and who approved.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 reads UBL and PDF invoices to line level and posts and approves one-to-one matches with order or receipt.
AFAS Scan & herken turns a PDF into an e-invoice and finds the supplier by KvK, VAT number and IBAN; gaps are filled by hand.
Escalante Golf cut invoice processing from 2.5 minutes to 45 seconds per invoice with suggested coding reviewed by staff.
Measured touchless shares often disappoint because of own ledger accounts, VAT codes and exceptions.

risks: Goods receipts are not booked on time at the sites, so matches fail and the queue does not shrink
Too wide a tolerance lets overcharges through unseen
Many small suppliers still send PDFs, keeping capture errors in the flow
research_questions: What share of Noordhaven's invoices today has a purchase order and a goods receipt in AFAS?
What share of invoices arrive as UBL versus PDF, per supplier?
How many days after delivery do sites book goods receipts?
What match rate does AFAS reach on three months of past invoices in a test environment?

tasks.short: Post debits and credits in AFAS and keep the Excel totals that check them.

today.trigger: Daily batches of approved invoices, receipts and bank lines waiting to be posted.
steps: Post approved invoices and memorial entries in AFAS Profit
Export balances to Excel to check totals per ledger and cost centre
Correct wrong postings with a reversal entry
Update control totals for the month-end file
drudgery: Rebuilding the same Excel control sheets every month
Keying memorial entries that repeat each month
today.time_sinks: Re-checking totals between AFAS and Excel and finding the cause of small differences.

lenses.faster: Recurring entries and control totals become standing AFAS entries and Power BI checks, so the bookkeeper only reviews the differences flagged; Excel rebuild work disappears.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS extract runs balance checks per ledger; any break against the expected total opens a task for the bookkeeper.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: ledger balances checked daily instead of at month end, so the close starts with clean books; demand grows because the Controller wants a shorter close.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the Excel totals sheet; bookkeepers want to spend the time on fixing root causes of wrong postings.
lenses.options: No real scenarios here; posting is right or wrong.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from keying to keeping a list of standing entries and daily checks up to date; slightly more expert, with the right to add recurring entries within an agreed list.
reach: Prepare the month-end balance checks the Accountant does today, learning accruals and the closing calendar

tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a correct-looking posting belongs to the wrong cost centre or site, and knowing the business event behind an odd balance.
tasks.pattern_why: Debit and credit logic and control totals are fixed rules; AFAS and a Power BI check can run them without a model.

steps: Recurring entries post on their schedule in AFAS
Power BI compares ledger balances with expected totals and last period
Breaks over a threshold create a task in the bookkeeper's list
Bookkeeper corrects and notes the cause
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves every correcting entry; new recurring entries need Controller approval.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS journal with entry author and Power BI check history.

evidence.claim: Standard accounting software posts recurring entries and the checks can be written as rules.
Every AP decision should be logged with its data when AP runs with people on exceptions.

risks: Power BI extract is only nightly, so same-day errors stay hidden
Standing entries keep running after the underlying contract ended
research_questions: How many hours a month go into Excel control sheets today?
Which memorial entries repeat every month and could be standing entries?
How often do audit adjustments trace back to wrong postings in the year?

tasks.short: Code invoices and costs to the right ledger, VAT code, site and cost centre.

today.trigger: An invoice without a purchase order (energy, repairs, agency hours, subscriptions) needs coding.
steps: Read the invoice and decide what it is for
Pick ledger account, VAT code, site and cost centre in AFAS
Check last month's coding for the same supplier
Ask the budget holder when unclear
drudgery: Looking up how the same supplier was coded before
Choosing VAT codes for reverse-charge and foreign suppliers
today.time_sinks: Non-PO invoices and unclear ones that need an email to a site manager.

lenses.faster: A coding proposal based on supplier history and invoice text is filled in; the bookkeeper confirms or corrects, so most invoices take seconds instead of minutes.
lenses.autonomous: Capture triggers the proposal; suppliers with stable coding history above a confidence level post without touch, the rest wait for confirmation.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the FP&A Analysts: costs coded consistently per site and activity, so they can forecast warehouse costs per site; demand grows when coding is cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses looking up past codings; bookkeepers want more time on the hard VAT and cross-border cases.
lenses.options: For unclear invoices, two coding options with their VAT effect help the bookkeeper choose.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the coding rules per supplier and the VAT code table and decides when a supplier may post untouched; more expert in VAT.
reach: VAT return preparation done by the Accountant, learning reverse-charge and intra-EU rules

tasks.human_edge: Judging what a vague invoice is really for, applying VAT on unusual transactions, and knowing site-specific practice.
tasks.pattern_why: Turning free invoice text into a checkable ledger, VAT and cost-centre proposal is one model call inside the AFAS workflow.

in_practice.trigger: Invoice captured in AFAS without a matching purchase order.
steps: Model reads invoice text and supplier coding history
Proposes ledger, VAT code, site and cost centre with a confidence score
Bookkeeper confirms or corrects in AFAS
Corrections feed back into the supplier's coding history
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper confirms each proposal before posting, except suppliers released by the Controller for untouched posting.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS posting history with proposal, final coding and who confirmed.

evidence.claim: Coding is suggested from vendor history for staff to review and confirm.
Own ledger accounts, VAT codes and exceptions per administration block touchless processing.
On a Peppol seller's reading, buyers must report intra-EU and reverse-charge purchases within 5 days of receipt under ViDA.

risks: Wrong VAT code repeated at scale
Past coding errors learned as rules
research_questions: What share of invoices has no purchase order?
How consistent is past coding per supplier?
How many VAT corrections came out of the last audit?

tasks.short: Move figures from agency portals, bank files and Excel sheets into AFAS.

today.trigger: Weekly agency hour statements, monthly sub-ledger summaries or spreadsheet lists that must go into the ledger.
steps: Download hours and invoices from the three staffing agency portals
Rework them in Excel to the AFAS import layout
Import or key the lines into AFAS
Check totals against the source
drudgery: Reformatting three different portal exports every week
today.time_sinks: Each agency has its own file layout, and layouts change without warning.

lenses.faster: Fixed import scripts per agency and per source turn exports into AFAS import files; the bookkeeper only checks the control totals.
lenses.autonomous: A new file in the agency portal or SharePoint folder triggers conversion and import; a failed total check stops the import and notifies the bookkeeper.
lenses.ambitious: A group served for the first time: flex worker costs per site and week visible to site managers in Power BI, instead of one month later; demand grows during peak season.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses reformatting portal exports; bookkeepers want time to question agencies about the numbers.
lenses.options: No real scenarios; it is a conversion.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains import mappings and agrees file layouts with agencies; a bit more technical.
reach: Agency data deliveries now handled by the HR Administrator, learning the agency contract terms

tasks.human_edge: Spotting that a source file is incomplete or from the wrong period, and settling layout issues with agency contacts.
tasks.pattern_why: File conversions follow fixed mappings; scripts built with AI coding run without a model.

in_practice.trigger: New export file in the agency portal or SharePoint drop folder.
steps: Script checks layout and period
Converts to the AFAS import format
Compares totals with the source
Imports into AFAS or stops and notifies
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper reviews the import summary; failed checks need a person to release.
in_practice.logs_to: Import log in SharePoint plus AFAS import batch.

evidence.claim: Mapping-based file conversion and import is routine software work.

risks: Agency changes layout and the script misreads columns
Portal access depends on personal logins
research_questions: Do the three agencies offer a stable export or API?
How many hours a week go into reformatting?
How often do import errors reach the ledger today?

tasks.short: Reconcile bank, supplier and customer accounts and report the differences.

today.trigger: Daily Rabobank statements and supplier statements; month end.
steps: Import Rabobank CAMT.053 statement into AFAS
Match open lines by hand that AFAS didn't match
Compare supplier statements with the AP ledger
List differences in Excel and send to the Controller
drudgery: Searching for which invoices a combined payment covers
Ticking supplier statements line by line
today.time_sinks: Combined payments without reference and supplier statements in different layouts.

lenses.faster: AFAS matching rules clear most bank lines; for the rest a model proposes which invoices a payment covers and why, and the bookkeeper confirms.
lenses.autonomous: Statement import triggers rule matching; unmatched lines get a proposed explanation and wait in the queue.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: supplier statements reconciled monthly for all key suppliers, not only at year end; demand grows because it cuts audit adjustments.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses scrolling for a combined payment; bookkeepers want time to fix the reasons (missing references, customers paying wrongly).
lenses.options: For a combined payment, two or three allocation options help decide which invoices to close.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns match rules and tolerances and reports recurring difference causes to the Controller.
reach: Customer payment allocation questions handled by the Credit and Collections Officer

tasks.human_edge: Judging an allocation when a customer underpaid, and knowing when a difference points to fraud or an error.
tasks.pattern_why: Rules do the matching; one model call explains each unmatched line in a checkable proposal.

steps: AFAS matches on reference, IBAN, invoice number and amounts
Model proposes allocation for unmatched lines with reasoning
Bookkeeper confirms or rejects
Open differences listed for the Controller

evidence.claim: AFAS matches CAMT.053 lines on reference, IBAN, invoice number and oldest-first sums; misses go to a person.

risks: Wrong allocation confirmed in a hurry
research_questions: What share of bank lines does AFAS match today?
How many hours a week go into unmatched lines?
How many supplier statements are reconciled per year now?

tasks.short: Check agency invoices against hours, post payroll journals, pay g-rekening share.

today.trigger: Weekly agency invoices and the monthly payroll run from the Payroll Specialist.
steps: Compare agency invoices with approved hours per site
Split the payment between the agency's normal and g-rekening
Post the payroll journal from AFAS payroll to the ledger
Prepare the wage tax and net salary payments
drudgery: Checking hours and rates line by line
Calculating the g-rekening share by hand
today.time_sinks: Hour differences between agency invoices and site approvals in peak season.

lenses.faster: Rules compare agency invoices with approved hours and CAO rates and calculate the g-rekening share; only differences reach a person.
lenses.autonomous: An agency invoice triggers the check against approved hours; matched invoices go into the payment run with the split, differences go to the bookkeeper.
lenses.ambitious: A group served for the first time: weekly checks on every flex worker invoice in peak season, with 150 to 300 flex workers, reducing liability risk under inlenersaansprakelijkheid.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses hour-by-hour comparing; bookkeepers want time to settle disputes with agencies.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper becomes the owner of agency invoice controls and liability documents, with more say on holding payment.
reach: Collecting agency payment-behaviour statements now done irregularly by HR Administrator
Payroll journal checks of the Payroll Specialist

tasks.human_edge: Settling hour disputes with agencies and site managers and judging liability risk.
tasks.pattern_why: Hours, rates and the g-rekening share follow written rules.

steps: Compare invoice lines with approved hours
Check rates against contract
Calculate g-rekening share
Send differences to bookkeeper
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves each invoice with differences; Controller approves the payment run.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS invoice history and SharePoint liability folder.

evidence.claim: Noordhaven can be held liable for agencies' unpaid wage tax and VAT and limits this via payment-behaviour statements, records and paying into the g-rekening.

risks: Approved hours missing at the sites
research_questions: Do sites approve hours in a system the check can read?
What share of agency invoices differ from hours today?
Are current payment-behaviour statements on file for all three agencies?

tasks.short: Send customer invoices, statements and reminders from AFAS.

today.trigger: End of week or month for warehousing and transport services.
steps: Collect billable services and rates
Create invoices in AFAS
Check against the customer contract
Send invoices and monthly statements
today.time_sinks: Contract rate checks and corrections after customer complaints.

lenses.faster: AFAS builds invoices from billable data and contract rates; statements and reminders are sent on schedule.
lenses.autonomous: Period end triggers invoice runs; invoices outside expected ranges go to the bookkeeper.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to customers: weekly invoices with detail per site, so customers dispute less and pay faster; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses sending statements by hand; bookkeepers want to resolve billing disputes.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns billing rules and contract rates in AFAS.
reach: Reminders now sent by the Credit and Collections Officer

tasks.pattern_why: Invoice amounts follow contract rates and rules.

steps: Collect billable data
Apply contract rates
Send invoices
Flag outliers

evidence.claim: Billing from contract rates is standard software work.

research_questions: Where does billable service data come from today?
How many invoices get corrected after sending?
Does DSO drop with weekly invoicing?

tasks.short: Make purchase orders and check expense claims with receipts.

today.trigger: Request from a site or an expense claim.
steps: Receive request or claim by email
Create a purchase order in AFAS
Check receipts against policy
Post and send for approval

lenses.faster: A model reads receipts and requests and fills in the claim or order; the bookkeeper checks.
lenses.autonomous: Submitted receipt triggers reading and policy check; exceptions go to the bookkeeper.
lenses.ambitious: A group served for the first time: drivers and night shift staff submit receipts by phone and get paid within days.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses keying receipts; bookkeepers want to improve the expense policy.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the policy checks.
reach: Purchase request handling done by site managers

tasks.pattern_why: Reading a receipt into fields is one model call.

steps: Model reads receipt
Policy rules check
Bookkeeper approves exceptions
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves each claim outside policy.

research_questions: How many claims a month?
Do drivers have a way to submit receipts?

role.altitude: From keying and matching invoices to owning match rules, tolerances, supplier data and agency invoice controls.
reach: Payment allocation for the Credit and Collections Officer
role.ceiling_note: Limited by data quality at the sites and supplier invoice formats.
role.ambitious_version: Daily clean books and checks on every flex worker invoice, so the month closes in days.
